issues.description: Title/CHANGELOG say 'single_network_interface' but PR description says 'multiple_network_interfaces' — naming is muddled.
issues.detail: The check folder, file, and CHANGELOG entry use 'single_network_interface' while the PR title and description refer to 'multiple_network_interfaces'. Pick one and make it the data: the check name should describe what it asserts. Naming carries the data structure for human readers; inconsistency here will leak into docs and search.

issues.description: GKE exemption keyed on a name prefix is the wrong data structure.
issues.detail: Detecting GKE-managed instances by `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` is string-sniffing that any user can spoof or unintentionally match. The right data is the GKE-managed label (`goog-gke-node`) or the managed-instance-group reference from the API. Capture that field in the Instance model and key the exemption off it. Data dominates.

issues.description: ip_forward / network-appliance exemption mentioned in metadata but not implemented.
issues.detail: The Notes call out network virtual appliances as legitimate multi-NIC, and `ip_forward` already exists on Instance. Either honor it (MANUAL when `ip_forward=True` and multi-NIC) or drop the claim. Right now the data is present but unused — a small composable signal left on the floor.

issues.description: NetworkInterface is a 3-field bag — fine, but `public_ip` already lives at Instance level redundantly.
issues.detail: The new NetworkInterface struct stores name/network/subnetwork while `public_ip` continues to be computed by a parallel loop and stored on Instance. Move accessConfigs/natIP into NetworkInterface too, then derive `public_ip` from `any(nic.public_ip for nic in instance.network_interfaces)`. One pass, one source of truth, the algorithm becomes self-evident.

issues.description: `interface_count == 0` branch reports PASS — semantically wrong for a 'single interface' check.
issues.detail: When `len(network_interfaces) == 0` the code falls through with the default `status='PASS'` and a status_extended saying 'has no network interfaces'. A VM with zero NICs is not 'single network interface'; it's a degenerate/unknown case. Either keep PASS but say so explicitly, or mark MANUAL. The data shape should drive the status, not default-through.

review.summary: The check is small and the data structure addition (NetworkInterface list on Instance) is the right move — data dominates, and now the algorithm is a one-liner. Two real issues: the GKE exemption uses string-prefix sniffing instead of the actual GKE label that the API provides, and the naming is inconsistent between 'single' and 'multiple' across title, folder, and CHANGELOG. Smaller cleanups: fold the existing parallel `public_ip` loop into the new NetworkInterface struct so there's one pass over the data, honor `ip_forward` for the network-appliance exemption the metadata promises, and don't silently PASS the zero-NIC degenerate case. Overall SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE with one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE around GKE detection.
